title: Minimum Split Into Subarrays With GCD Greater Than One
summary: Given an array of positive integers, divide it into the smallest number of disjoint subarrays where the GCD of each subarray is greater than 1.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, divide it into the smallest number of disjoint subarrays where the GCD of each subarray is greater than 1. Each element must belong to exactly one subarray, and the GCD of each subarray must be strictly greater than 1.
constraints: Partition the entire positive array into contiguous nonempty subarrays.
Every group’s greatest common divisor must be strictly greater than one.
Return the minimum number of groups.
reference_solution:
def minimum_gcd_subarray_splits(nums):
    from math import gcd
    groups=1;common=0
    for value in nums:
        common=gcd(common,value)
        if common==1:groups+=1;common=value
    return groups

def minimum_gcd_subarray_splits(nums):
    from math import gcd
    groups=0;common=0
    for value in nums:
        common=gcd(common,value)
        if common==1:groups+=1;common=value
    return groups
hints: Extend the current group while maintaining its running GCD.
When adding a value makes the GCD one, end the previous group and begin a new group at that value.
Otherwise keep extending because delaying a split cannot reduce future feasibility.
Once a prefix GCD reaches one it can never increase by adding values, so a split is mandatory; splitting at the latest possible point minimizes the group count.
